correctness.rationale: With order-preserving coordinates, keep the odd coordinates and replace each even coordinate x_i by 1−x_i; this is affine unimodular, and transforms the cover inequalities into y_i+y_{i+1}≤1. It is not an assertion that the general transfer map is affine. For n≥2 the edge inequalities and nonnegativity give all bounds; for n=1 retain the interval upper bound y_1≤1, implicit in the later segment check but omitted from the displayed path inequality list. At an independent-set vertex S, the active facets are exactly the zero-coordinate facets and incident edge facets, so for n≥3 there are n plus the number of selected interior vertices. Any such interior vertex makes the point nonsimple. Otherwise coordinate normals and one endpoint replacement per selected endpoint are unimodular by subtraction, even at n=3 with both endpoints selected. The n=1,2 polytopes are a unimodular segment and triangle. The degree is the number E_n of linear extensions by unimodular triangulation; compactness and torus-orbit additivity give Euler characteristic equal to the number F_{n+2} of independent sets (include/exclude the last vertex). Differentiating A=sec z+tan z gives A'=(A²+1)/2; the k=1,n binomial terms yield E_{n+2}≥(n+1)E_n for n≥2. Since F_{n+4}<3F_{n+2}, the positive gaps at n=5,6 propagate by parity, and n=1–4 are strictly negative. Independent /workspace/branches/review02_order_check.py directly enumerated filters and checked the active normal determinants in order-polytope coordinates through n=16 and counted extensions by permutations through n=9. This is bounded regression evidence, not the general proof.
